newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades defensive late as buyers retreat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades defensive late as buyers retreat.

text.p: U.S. domestic crudes adopted a defensive posture late Wednesday after bearish builds in crude stocks were reported in latest inventory data.
Refinery problems in the Midwest also contributed to the overall bearish tone, keeping potential buyers sidelined.
Traders said grades were also hit by seasonal downturns in demand, ahead of the approaching year-end.
But outrights chalked up gains on the back of heating oil, which rose on reports distillate stocks had grown.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $22.70-80 a barrel, up about 10 cents from Tuesday.
The Dec/Jan WTI spread narrowed to 15-16 cents from about 22 cents earlier, pressing down values for WTI/Cushing Posting Plus which drifted to postings plus $1.88 from $1.93.
Other light, sweet grades lost momentum throughout the day marking perception refinery demand was on the wane here and in Europe, now that product shortages were being alleviated.
A softer Dated Brent level of Dec Brent minus 57 cents for a Nov 14-16 cargo, subsequently hurt Louisiana crudes.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded to WTI plus 48 to 55 cents, but revived to 57 cents later. The grade had traded at 67/68 cents overnight.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was confirmed traded at plus 57-58 cents, down from 71 cts premium.
A strong motivation for selling came from rumors Shell would be a strong seller due to a drop in capacity at its Wood River, Illinois refinery, hurt by a fire on Tuesday.
The major later emerged as a buyer instead, causing offers to pull back from earlier levels, traders said.
Midland/WTI dropped to minus one cent, compared with the previous level of 3-5 cents above the marker.
Heavy sours were also weaker, with West Texas Sour done at minus $1.65, down from minus $1.57-$1.60 Tuesday.
Eugene Island also dived to minus $1.35, losing 15 cents.
